heading: Organize the property question before requesting a tax review
body:
A property tax discussion is more productive when the records explain the decision. State whether you are buying, improving, changing use, refinancing, or selling. Give the expected timing and identify the owners and entities involved. Similar-looking properties can create different questions when their histories differ.

Prepare the closing statement, existing depreciation schedule, major improvement records, loan information, prior reporting, and any relevant study. Separate amounts you can support from estimates. If a document is missing, name it and explain who is obtaining it instead of silently replacing it with a round number.

For a fictional renovation, a single contractor total may cover equipment, building work, and repairs. The reviewer needs scope and timing to evaluate the treatment. Asking the contractor for usable detail while the work is active can be easier than reconstructing it during filing season.

Confirm the engagement scope, person responsible for the return, implementation steps, and required follow-up. Use the professional profile and firm resources to understand the service path; determine the treatment of your property through a fact-specific review.
